question: Where is Morgan Stanley investing in technology for its advisors?

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley says it is making ongoing investments in its world-class platform, including investments to support its advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of its workplace channel. (MS-TR-2025Q2#3)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley names LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform, which focuses on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors, as one of its early AI use cases. (MS-TR-2025Q3#8)
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley names Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data, as one of its early AI use cases. (MS-TR-2025Q3#8)
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley names the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code, as one of its early AI use cases. (MS-TR-2025Q3#8)
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states that its scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools. (MS-TR-2026Q3#16)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest in deepening its competitive moats in areas such as its expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash. (MS-TR-2025Q3#13)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it has put significant resources toward lending products, including digital tools, digital enhancements, and using automation to help with the paper backlog associated with various lending products. (MS-TR-2026Q1#36)
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it was overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth, including some of the work it did with OpenAI. (MS-TR-2026Q3#49)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states that the insights from its size and scale allow its financial advisors to tailor advice and equip its own tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals. (MS-TR-2026Q3#34)
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest across its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people. (MS-TR-2026Q3#8)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it has been investing in its processes and systems across the technology side, in better understanding its data, and in better servicing its clients. (MS-TR-2024Q4#44)

Morgan Stanley: In 2025Q3, among its early AI use cases (some live and some in pilot), Morgan Stanley states it has LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform focused on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors. (MS-TR-2025Q3#8)
Morgan Stanley: In 2026Q2, Morgan Stanley states it is investing in products like LeadIQ that will allow it to match individuals with advisers. (MS-TR-2026Q2#23)

Morgan Stanley: In 2025Q4, Morgan Stanley states it is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending. (MS-TR-2025Q4#9)

Morgan Stanley: In 2026Q1, Morgan Stanley states its wealth team is focused on AI 'co-piloting' where a financial adviser has historical context of past client interactions, and that the firm is building 'corridors' or 'super agents' to drive efficiency and effectiveness across the wealth portfolio. (MS-TR-2026Q1#43)
Morgan Stanley: In 2025Q3, Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest and deepen its competitive moats through an expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets. (MS-TR-2025Q3#13)
Morgan Stanley: In 2025Q3, Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash. (MS-TR-2025Q3#13)
Morgan Stanley: In 2026Q3, Morgan Stanley states its scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools. (MS-TR-2026Q3#16)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases include LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with its financial advisors. (MS-TR-2025Q3#8)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's CEO described 'co-piloting' for financial advisers, with Jed Finn under Andy Saperstein spending time on 'corridors or super agents' to drive efficiency and effectiveness across the wealth portfolio. (MS-TR-2026Q1#43)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley is leveraging technology to improve automation and facilitate client acquisition openings, as well as increasing education with its advisors and clients. (MS-TR-2025Q4#21)

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley has ongoing investments in automation and AI, and in assessing where it wants its people over the next five to ten years, in the context of a reduction in XFA headcount. (MS-TR-2025Q1#73)

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick describes AI as a top priority for the firm's advisory role, saying the firm is now 'double overweight' on AI and that it is existentially important that Morgan Stanley be viewed as a trusted adviser in the middle of the ecosystem. (MS-TR-2026Q3#49)

Morgan Stanley: CFO Sharon Yeshaya describes early AI use cases, including LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with financial advisors, as well as DevGen AI (enhancing developer efficiency) and Parable (an interactive tool analyzing and summarizing data). (MS-TR-2025Q3#8)
Morgan Stanley: CFO Sharon Yeshaya states the firm's scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools. (MS-TR-2026Q3#16)

Morgan Stanley: CEO Ted Pick states the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending. (MS-TR-2025Q4#9)

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick describes the ability to protect client assets and a resiliency theme as critical to clients, and states that although it is a people business, technology can help do a lot of the early work for financial advisers. (MS-TR-2026Q3#35)

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick describes the firm's 'world-class technology, world-class cyber defense and then the best trusted advisers sitting with the client' as the 'secret sauce,' including for the wealth management and financial adviser. (MS-TR-2026Q1#44)

Morgan Stanley: CEO Ted Pick states the firm continues to invest in Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology, with growth plans embedding increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and client base. (MS-TR-2025Q4#8)
Morgan Stanley: CFO Sharon Yeshaya states the firm continues to invest across its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people. (MS-TR-2026Q3#8)

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick states cyber resiliency is a top priority across all of the firm's businesses, and that AI will bring efficiency and effectiveness that should not be dismissed as it transforms the firm. (MS-TR-2026Q1#66)
Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick states the firm has built advantages against its advisor-led platform that make technology a differentiator in its favor. (MS-TR-2026Q3#32)

Morgan Stanley: CEO Ted Pick describes the early digital asset transformation in wealth, including a partnership with Zero Hash, expansion into crypto and tokenized asset capabilities, and continued work on the E*TRADE platform for the active self-directed community. (MS-TR-2025Q4#72)
